answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when a randomly selected audit proves the agent duplicated a fulfilled task or fabricated credentials. Because audits sample across the whole summit rather than trusting a polished terrace of profiles, spawning hundreds of identities multiplies the attacker’s exposure: each must tie up capital, and any caught identity loses its stake. Honest agents can earn nectar from completed work, while fake ones face a measurable cost instead of free account creation.
